questions.stem: In this heart diagram, which valve prevents backflow of blood into the left atrium during ventricular systole?

explanation.summary: The mitral (left atrioventricular) valve closes during ventricular systole to stop regurgitation from the left ventricle back into the left atrium. Its closure, along with the tricuspid valve, contributes to the S1 heart sound.
explanation.whyCorrect: The mitral (left atrioventricular) valve closes during ventricular systole to stop regurgitation from the left ventricle back into the left atrium. Its closure, along with the tricuspid valve, contributes to the S1 heart sound.

questions.stem: In this cardiac cycle diagram, the aortic valve opens at the moment when ventricular pressure does what relative to aortic pressure?

explanation.summary: The aortic valve opens only once left ventricular pressure exceeds aortic diastolic pressure (~80 mmHg here), beginning the ejection phase. It closes again when ventricular pressure falls back below aortic pressure, generating S2.
explanation.whyCorrect: The aortic valve opens only once left ventricular pressure exceeds aortic diastolic pressure (~80 mmHg here), beginning the ejection phase. It closes again when ventricular pressure falls back below aortic pressure, generating S2.

questions.stem: The S1 heart sound marked on this pressure/phonocardiogram diagram is generated primarily by the closure of which valves?

explanation.summary: S1 coincides with the onset of ventricular systole and is produced by closure of the atrioventricular (mitral and tricuspid) valves as ventricular pressure rises above atrial pressure. S2 is generated later by semilunar valve closure.
explanation.whyCorrect: S1 coincides with the onset of ventricular systole and is produced by closure of the atrioventricular (mitral and tricuspid) valves as ventricular pressure rises above atrial pressure. S2 is generated later by semilunar valve closure.

questions.stem: In the normal S2 shown at the top, why does the A2-P2 split widen during inspiration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The mitral valve closes earlier during inspiration

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased venous return delays pulmonic valve closure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Systemic vascular resistance falls during inspiration

explanation.summary: Inspiration lowers intrathoracic pressure, augmenting venous return to the right heart. The larger right ventricular volume prolongs right ventricular ejection, delaying pulmonic (P2) closure and thereby widening the physiologic splitting of S2.
explanation.whyCorrect: Inspiration lowers intrathoracic pressure, augmenting venous return to the right heart. The larger right ventricular volume prolongs right ventricular ejection, delaying pulmonic (P2) closure and thereby widening the physiologic splitting of S2.
